question: What makes old shoebox halls like Vienna's Musikverein, opened in 1870, sound better than most modern halls?
options: Their curved ceilings focus the sound
Near side walls send sound in sideways
answer: Near side walls send sound in sideways. Research from the late 1960s, by Harold Marshall and later Michael Barron, found that early reflections reaching the ears from the sides make listeners feel wrapped in sound. A narrow hall does it by shape. Thin wood panelling tends to soak up bass rather than sing along.
move: When the best examples share two features, test each one alone.
ask: When two things come together in a success I admire, have I tried to work out which one really does the work?
trap: Great old halls are full of wood, so the wood gets the credit.
reference: Barron, Auditorium Acoustics and Architectural Design, E & FN Spon, 1993
